Hi Priya and Liam,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Attached is our latest DPA with the redlines we discussed — the change log focuses on two asks you raised: (1) explicit carve-out preventing use of Customer Data for model training/model improvement, and (2) subprocessor transparency and 30-day notice for new subprocessors that will process Customer Data.

Two quick clarifications we need from your side before we can finalize:
- For the training carve-out, do you want a blanket prohibition on any use of Customer Data for model training, or would you accept a scoped allowance for aggregated/anonymized telemetry that cannot be traced back to an individual or account?
- For cross-border transfers, you mentioned EU SCCs on the call — is your legal team comfortable with Redwood acting as a data processor using SCCs, with KMS controls for key management?

I copied Marissa from Legal for review. I can pull the redlines into DocuSign once we align on the carve-out language. Attached: DPA_FinServ_Redlines_v3.pdf and Definitions_Carveouts.docx.

Next steps: if you can confirm carve-out preference by end of day Wednesday, I will prepare the DocuSign envelope and send for signature.

Best,
Alex Martinez

Alex,

Thanks for sending this over and for the clear summary. We reviewed the redlines with our security and privacy group and have a couple of follow-ups captured in the attached annotated DPA. High level:
- We are asking for a prohibition on using any Customer Data for model training or improving models that could materially benefit the provider unless explicit prior consent is obtained. Aggregated telemetry is OK if it is irreversibly anonymized and cannot be re-identified.
- For subprocessors, we need a 30-calendar-day notice plus the right to object; if we object, you should provide an option for us to have the data processed by an alternate subprocessor or within our dedicated environment.
- For transfers, we will require SCCs + a written attestation about key residency (EU keys for EU-origin data) or an approved KMS configuration.

See the attached PDF for inline comments. I'll get Legal to follow up directly if they want any additional edits.

Priya Shah
Head of IT Risk & Privacy
FinServ Solutions

Marissa/Neha/Markus,

Forwarding Priya's note from FinServ. They want a strict no-training clause unless we have explicit consent, plus a 30-day notice and objection right for subprocessors, and SCCs + key residency/KMS attestation for transfers.

Two asks:
1) Can Legal/Privacy draft a tight, customer-friendly 'no-training' clause that still allows Redwood to use irreversibly aggregated metrics for service-level monitoring and capacity planning? Example we used for another customer included language around 'non-personally identifiable, aggregated telemetry' with a prohibition on incorporating Customer Data into model weights.
2) For subprocessors, can we accept a 30-calendar-day notice and an objection right that triggers either an alternate hosting option or negotiation, without committing to a full termination right?

I want to avoid overcommitting on KMS key residency unless we can offer controlled options (e.g., EU-only key wrap for EU data). Please advise redline text and I will send back to Priya.

Thanks,
Alex

Alex,

Attached below is suggested redline language that balances FinServ's ask with our operational requirements. Please confirm if you want me to insert these into the PDF and produce a final DocuSign envelope.

Suggested clause for 'Use of Customer Data' (proposed):
1) Provider shall not use Customer Data to train, tune or improve Provider models, model weights, or model architectures that are used to serve other customers, unless Customer has given explicit written consent for such use.
2) Notwithstanding the foregoing, Provider may collect and use aggregated, irreversibly anonymized telemetry and usage metrics that cannot be traced back to an individual or account for the sole purposes of service monitoring, capacity planning, and product analytics, provided such telemetry does not contain Customer Data as defined in Section X.

For subprocessors:
- Provider will provide Customer with at least 30 calendar days written notice prior to engaging a new subprocessor that will process Customer Data. Customer may object in writing within 15 calendar days. If Customer objects, Provider shall use commercially reasonable efforts to provide alternatives, including the option to process Customer Data within an approved Dedicated environment or to identify an alternate subprocessor.

On SCCs and KMS:
- We can accept SCCs for EU transfers. For key residency, we can offer EU key-wrapping and attestations for EU-origin datasets when requested via an SOC change order and with an associated runbook. That requires an SOW amendment for key management responsibilities.

If this looks good, I will: (a) insert into the annotated PDF, (b) create a clean redline accept/decline summary, and (c) draft the DocuSign envelope text.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Privacy Counsel
Redwood Inference
